en: Reductionism, Complexity, and the Question of Simplicity
ja: 還元主義、複雑性、そして単純さの問題
zh: 还原论、复杂性与简单性问题

p.src: Susskind opens with a deliberately familiar philosophical slogan: big things are made of little things, and little things are made of littler things. He then adds the more ambitious version of the same idea, the one that really matters for fundamental physics: as one descends through deeper layers, the objects should become not only smaller but also simpler. His metaphor is that houses are made of bricks, and nobody mistakes a house for a brick. The brick is smaller, but it is also simpler.

ja: サスキンドは、意図的に親しみやすい哲学的スローガンから始める。大きなものは小さなものからできており、小さなものはさらに小さなものからできている、というものである。次に彼は同じ考えのより野心的な版、基礎物理学にとって本当に重要な版を付け加える。より深い層へと降りていくにつれて、対象はより小さくなるだけでなく、より単純にもなるはずだ、というものである。彼の比喩は、家はレンガからできており、家をレンガと間違える人はいない、というものである。レンガはより小さいが、より単純でもある。
zh: Susskind以一个刻意熟悉的哲学口号开场：大的东西由小的东西构成，小的东西由更小的东西构成。随后他补充了同一思想的更具雄心的版本，也就是对基础物理真正重要的那个版本：当人们深入更深的层次时，对象不仅应当变得更小，还应当变得更简单。他的比喻是，房子由砖块构成，而没有人会把房子误认为砖块。砖块更小，但它也更简单。

p.src:
The first move of the lecture is to confront that expectation with the actual state of particle physics. If reductionism were delivering increasing simplicity in that strong sense, one might expect present-day elementary particle physics to be close to economical. Instead, Susskind emphasizes that even before quantum gravity enters, the bookkeeping already looks messy. In the lecture these are rough counts, but the roughness is part of the point: $\begin{aligned}
N_{\mathrm{species}}&\sim 75,\\
N_{\mathrm{independent}}&\sim 10\text{--}20,\\
N_{\mathrm{parameters}}&\sim 20.
\end{aligned}$ Even this is not the end of the story. The Standard Model does not contain gravity, does not explain dark matter, does not supply the extra structure needed for inflation, and carries a severe fine-tuning problem. Adding the usual repair mechanisms only increases the count. Supersymmetry is the lecture’s example. At the time of the lecture, many physicists hoped that the Large Hadron Collider would expose superpartners; Susskind stresses that the corresponding extension would introduce more than a hundred additional parameters rather than immediately simplifying the bookkeeping. His schematic message is $N_{\mathrm{parameters}}^{\mathrm{extended}} \sim 200.$ These numbers are deliberately rough and historical. They serve the argument that a deeper description need not look simpler at the level of its particle inventory and measured constants.

p.src: This quantitative complaint is not yet Susskind’s main thesis. It is the prelude. The deeper claim, and the one that drives the rest of the lecture, is that modern quantum field theory and string theory do not obviously support a unique, coupling-independent distinction between the bricks and the houses. p.src: One starts with a field theory of fermions. The fermion field is denoted by $\psi$. Two nearby fermions can form a bosonic composite, and the corresponding bosonic field is denoted by $\phi$. At first sight the hierarchy seems straightforward: $\psi$ is basic, while $\phi$ is a composite or effective variable. In the lecture the boson is introduced exactly this way, as a field that creates bound pairs of fermions.

What was discovered, however, is that the same theory can be rewritten from the opposite starting point. One may begin with the bosonic field $\phi$, and then the fermion no longer appears as a point-like constituent. Instead it appears as a kink of the bosonic field, an extended configuration in which $\phi$ interpolates smoothly between two asymptotic values. The minimum mathematical content of the lecture is this asymptotic structure: $\phi(x\to -\infty)=\phi_-,
\qquad
\phi(x\to +\infty)=\phi_+.$ A convenient schematic representative is $\phi(x)\approx \frac{\phi_++\phi_-}{2}
+
\frac{\phi_+-\phi_-}{2}\tanh\!\left(\frac{x}{\ell}\right),$ where $\ell$ is the width of the transition region.

The point becomes sharper once a coupling is introduced. Susskind calls it $G$ in this example. The statement is not that the two descriptions are vaguely related, but that the efficiency of the two descriptions depends on the parameter regime: $\begin{aligned}G \ll 1
&\Rightarrow
\ell\text{ small, tight kink; }\psi\text{ efficient},\\
G \gg 1
&\Rightarrow
\ell\text{ large, broad kink; }\phi\text{ efficient}.\end{aligned}$ For small $G$, the kink is tight and the fermion looks like the simple object. As $G$ increases, the kink broadens and the fermion becomes less point-like. The bosonic variables then become the more economical ones.

p.src: The relevant control parameter is the fine-structure constant $\alpha$. In the lecture Susskind treats it heuristically as the square of the electric charge: $\alpha \sim e^2.$ He also gives a rough operational interpretation: it measures how readily an electron radiates, and he summarizes that strength by saying that an accelerated electron radiates on the order of $1/100$ photons in the relevant sense. In the lecture’s own rough numerical language, $\alpha \approx 10^{-2}.$ This is not intended as a precision convention; it is a pedagogical way of encoding that electric charge is weak.

p.src:
When $\alpha\ll 1$, the electron is the simple object. Its electric field is weak, its vacuum polarization cloud is dilute, and it looks almost point-like. The magnetic monopole is then the opposite: its field is enormous, its surroundings are violently distorted, and it is broad, complicated, and heavy. Susskind summarizes the situation in precisely this weak–strong style: $\begin{aligned}
\alpha \ll 1
&\Rightarrow \text{simple electron;}\\
&\phantom{\Rightarrow{}}\text{heavy, extended monopole},\\
\alpha \gg 1
&\Rightarrow \text{simple monopole;}\\
&\phantom{\Rightarrow{}}\text{heavy, structured electron}.
\end{aligned}$ The lecture does not derive a monopole mass formula. It does not need one. The point is qualitative. As $\alpha$ increases, the electron’s field strengthens and its structure grows, while the monopole shrinks and becomes lighter. Far beyond unity, the useful description is exchanged: the monopole is simple and the electron complicated.

zh: 听众提问: 如果还原论不是可靠的指南，为什么物理学家还依赖微积分？微积分似乎把系统分成任意小的部分。 (讲课时间: 00:21:21)

p.src: Response: Calculus asserts smooth variation; it does not identify the fundamental objects of a theory. Quantum fields fluctuate on every distance scale, producing an endless hierarchy rather than a final smooth layer at which one can decide once and for all what is elementary.

u.src: Response: Calculus asserts smooth variation; it does not identify the fundamental objects of a theory. Quantum fields fluctuate on every distance scale, producing an endless hierarchy rather than a final smooth layer at which one can decide once and for all what is elementary.

ja: 回答: 微積分は滑らかな変化を主張するが、理論の基本的対象を同定するものではない。量子場はあらゆる距離スケールで揺らぎ、何が要素的かを一度きりで決められる最終的な滑らかな層ではなく、終わりのない階層を生み出す。
zh: 回答: 微积分断言的是光滑变化；它并不指认理论的基本对象。量子场在每一个距离尺度上涨落，产生无尽的层级，而不是一个最终的、光滑的层次，让人可以在那里一劳永逸地判定什么是基本的。

p.src: The exchange continues with the suggestion that the hierarchy resembles a fractal. Susskind accepts the analogy, then sharpens it: quantum fields fluctuate on every scale and are therefore never smooth in the classical sense. This excessive variation is part of what makes quantum field theory mathematically difficult; ordinary calculus must be used with renormalized quantities rather than with a naively smooth microscopic field.

p.src:
The weak–strong story then repeats itself in string language. At small coupling the F-string is light, thin, and close to the original intuitive image of the fundamental object. The D-string is thick, heavy, and full of F-string structure. As the coupling grows, the F-string splits more readily; the cloud of daughter strings proliferates around it, and it becomes heavier and more complicated. At the same time the D-string has increasing difficulty emitting the now-heavy F-strings, so its surrounding structure thins out and it becomes lighter and more line-like. The lecture’s weak–strong map is therefore $\begin{aligned}g \ll 1
&\Rightarrow
\begin{gathered}
\text{F-string light and thin;}\\
\text{D-string heavy and structured},
\end{gathered}\\
g \sim 1
&\Rightarrow
\text{F-string and D-string comparable},\\
g \gg 1
&\Rightarrow
\begin{gathered}
\text{D-string light and thin;}\\
\text{F-string heavy and structured}.
\end{gathered}\end{aligned}$ Susskind remarks that around $g\sim 1$ the two descriptions cease to be sharply distinct. Beyond that point they effectively exchange roles. This is the string-theoretic version of the electron–monopole interchange, and its accepted name is S-duality.

p.src: The same exchange can be followed after a string closes into a loop. At weak coupling, a small F-string loop is a light particle-like excitation, while the corresponding D-string loop is heavy and complicated. At strong coupling their roles reverse: the D-string loop becomes the light description, and among the resulting light closed-string excitations is the graviton. The lecture uses this example to insist that even the identity of a familiar particle may depend on which side of the duality is used.

p.src: The lecture pushes the point one step further. In the idealized theory the coupling is not merely a number to be dialed by hand; it behaves like a field. Schematically, $g = g(x).$ Different regions of space can therefore favor different dual descriptions. In one region F-strings are the light variables; in another region D-strings are. In between, nothing is especially simple. That is why, for Susskind, string theory does not restore the simple reductionist picture. It radicalizes the ambiguity.

p.src: The same later discussion also motivates Susskind’s heuristic energy bookkeeping. He insists that the relevant energy is not merely the sum of free-particle contributions. One must also include interaction energy: $E_{\mathrm{tot}} = E_e + E_\gamma + E_{\mathrm{int}}.$ Here $E_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the crucial term. It is what lets the mass of the dressed electron include the energy associated with its surrounding field and virtual structure. The lecture does not turn this into a formal renormalized self-energy derivation. The point is heuristic but essential: the object’s mass already includes the interaction energy required to support the complicated cloud around it.

p.src: Response: One never starts with a bare electron and later attaches its Coulomb field. The observed electron is a dressed state, and its mass already includes field and interaction energy. In QED the total energy is not the free electron energy plus the free photon energy alone; the interaction term is indispensable. Calling the intermediate pairs virtual is useful, but the energy bookkeeping belongs to the complete interacting state.

ja: 回答: 裸の電子から始めて後からそのクーロン場を付けるということは決してない。観測される電子は着衣状態であり、その質量はすでに場と相互作用のエネルギーを含んでいる。QEDでは全エネルギーは自由電子のエネルギーと自由光子のエネルギーのみの和ではない。相互作用項が不可欠である。中間の対を仮想と呼ぶのは有用だが、エネルギーの計算は完全な相互作用状態に属する。
zh: 回答: 人们从来不是从一个裸电子开始，然后再附加上它的库仑场。被观测到的电子是一个缀饰态，其质量已经包括了场能和相互作用能。在QED中，总能量并不只是自由电子能量加上自由光子能量；相互作用项是不可或缺的。把中间粒子对称为虚的是有用的，但能量记账属于完整的相互作用态。

p.src: Up to this point the lecture has been telling a strong story about exchange: fermion versus boson, electron versus monopole, F-string versus D-string. The next step is more surprising. Susskind switches to a different version of string theory, one with even-dimensional D-branes rather than odd-dimensional ones. The distinction matters because in this theory there is no D-string to exchange with the F-string. One has D0-branes, D2-branes, D4-branes, and so on.

ja: ここまで、講義は交換について強い物語を語ってきた。フェルミオン対ボソン、電子対モノポール、F弦対D弦である。次の段階はより驚くべきものである。Susskindは弦理論の別のバージョンへと切り替える。奇数次元のDブレーンではなく、偶数次元のDブレーンを持つものである。この区別が重要であるのは、この理論にはF弦と交換すべきD弦が存在しないからである。D0ブレーン、D2ブレーン、D4ブレーンなどがある。
zh: 至此，讲座一直在讲述一个关于交换的强有力故事：费米子对玻色子、电子对磁单极子、F-弦对 D-弦。下一步更加令人惊讶。Susskind 转向弦理论的另一个版本，其中使用的是偶数维 D-膜，而不是奇数维的。这一区别很重要，因为在这个理论中没有可与 F-弦交换的 D-弦。人们有 D0-膜、D2-膜、D4-膜，等等。

p.src: The strong-coupling limit therefore cannot simply be a relabeling of one string as another. According to the lecture, something stranger happens: an extra spatial dimension becomes manifest. Susskind deliberately states this in the most dramatic form first — a new dimension materializes — and then immediately translates it into the more careful statement: a very small compact direction expands until it can no longer be ignored.

zh: 因此，强耦合极限不能简单地把一种弦重新标记为另一种弦。根据讲座，会发生更奇怪的事情：一个额外的空间维度变得显明。Susskind 故意先以最戏剧化的形式陈述这一点 — 一个新维度实体化 —，然后立即将其转化为更谨慎的陈述：一个非常小的紧致方向膨胀到不再能被忽略。

en: The peanut-butter sandwich
ja: ピーナッツバターサンドイッチ

p.src:
To picture the compact direction, Susskind uses the peanut-butter sandwich model: two infinitely thin pieces of bread, with real space between them. The special rule is that going out one side returns one to the other. In a conventional notation that the lecture describes pictorially rather than formally, one may write $y \sim y + 2\pi R.$ If $R$ is very small, observers living in the sandwich effectively describe their world as lower-dimensional. The key strong-coupling update is then $g\uparrow
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
R_{\mathrm{compact}}\uparrow.$ That is what Susskind means when he says that a new dimension of space appears: not that space is created from nothing, but that a previously tiny compact direction expands and becomes visible in the effective theory.

p.src: A D3-brane worldvolume

u.src: A D3-brane worldvolume
en: A D3-brane worldvolume

p.src: The first bridge uses a D3-brane. A D3-brane has three spatial dimensions, and an observer confined to it can easily mistake it for ordinary space. The brane can bend and fluctuate, while strings ending on it can join, split, and scatter. To an observer who sees only directions along the brane, each endpoint looks like a particle and the interactions among endpoints look like an ordinary quantum field theory.

ja: 最初の橋はD3ブレーンを用いる。D3ブレーンは三つの空間次元を持ち、それに閉じ込められた観測者はそれを通常の空間と容易に誤認しうる。ブレーンは曲がり揺らぐことができ、一方それに端点を持つ弦は結合し、分裂し、散乱しうる。ブレーンに沿った方向のみを見る観測者にとって、各端点は粒子のように見え、端点間の相互作用は通常の量子場理論のように見える。
zh: 第一座桥梁使用 D3-膜。一张 D3-膜有三个空间维度，被限制在其中的观测者很容易把它误认为普通空间。膜可以弯曲和涨落，而终止于其上的弦可以连接、分裂和散射。对于只看到沿膜方向的观测者来说，每个端点看起来像一个粒子，而端点之间的相互作用看起来像普通的量子场论。

p.src: This is one of the lecture’s most satisfying identifications. An F-string ending on the D3-brane appears to the worldvolume observer as an electric charge. A D-string ending on the same brane appears as a magnetic monopole. In other words, the duality between F-strings and D-strings becomes, on the D3-brane worldvolume, the electric–magnetic duality of ordinary field theory. What was earlier an analogy is now an explicit dictionary.

p.src:
A membrane may wrap either compact direction and look like a string from the non-compact directions. If $R_1$ and $R_2$ are the two circle radii, its effective tensions are $\begin{aligned}
T_{(1)}&=2\pi R_1 T_{\mathrm{M2}},\\
T_{(2)}&=2\pi R_2 T_{\mathrm{M2}},\\
\frac{T_{(1)}}{T_{(2)}}&=\frac{R_1}{R_2}.
\end{aligned}$ Thus unequal circle sizes produce unequal string tensions. With the shorter wrapping identified as the light F-string and the longer one as the heavy D-string, one may write schematically $g_s\sim \frac{R_{\mathrm{short}}}{R_{\mathrm{long}}},
\qquad
\frac{T_{\mathrm{D1}}}{T_{\mathrm{F1}}}\sim \frac{1}{g_s}.$

ja: まず、Susskindは、精密に制御された双対性は高度に理想化された超対称理論の特徴であり、そこではボソンとフェルミオンが正確に一致した質量で現れると警告する。彼の類推はニュートン力学における円軌道である。実際の惑星運動が完全な円で尽くされるからではなく、対称で数学的に扱いやすいから、まずそれを研究するのである。まったく同じように、超対称弦理論は、自然が示すよりも対称性が高いため、解析しやすいのである。
zh: 首先，Susskind 警告说，那些被精确控制的对偶性，是高度理想化的超对称理论的特征；在这些理论中，玻色子和费米子以完全匹配的质量出现。他将其类比为牛顿力学中的圆轨道：人们首先研究它们，是因为它们对称且数学上易于处理，而不是因为实际的行星运动可以被完美的圆穷尽。完全同样地，超对称弦理论之所以更容易分析，是因为它们比自然所显现的更为对称。

p.src: The idealization is nonetheless informative. A perfect circular orbit is not a realistic planetary system, but it displays features that survive in less symmetric orbits. Likewise, the supersymmetric examples show consistent ways in which quantum mechanics, gravity, and microscopic structure can fit together. Susskind’s deliberately sharp formulation is that the tractable string theories are not, literally, the theory of our world; their value is that they reveal phenomena likely to reappear in less symmetric and less tractable settings.

zh: 尽管如此，这种理想化仍具有启发性。一个完美的圆轨道并不是一个现实的行星系统，但它展示了在对称性较低的轨道中仍然存留的特征。同样地，超对称例子展示了量子力学、引力和微观结构能够相互协调的若干自洽方式。Susskind 刻意给出的尖锐表述是：那些易于处理的弦理论，字面上并不是关于我们世界的理论；它们的价值在于揭示了很可能在对称性较低、也更难以处理的情形中重新出现的现象。

p.src: Suppose, in the lecture’s schematic count, a six-dimensional compact space has roughly $500$ cycles and each cycle admits on the order of $10$ choices of wrapped branes, fluxes, or related structures. Then the number of constructions grows like $N_{\mathrm{vacua}} \sim 10^{500}.$ The lecture’s counting logic is elementary: $10 \times 10 \times \cdots \times 10 = 10^{500}$ with $500$ factors. The DNA analogy makes the same point in a more familiar register: $N_{\mathrm{DNA}}(500)=4^{500}.$ During the DNA comparison, an audience member checks that there are four alternatives along one strand: A, C, G, and T. The correction reinforces rather than changes the argument. A short list of local choices, repeated many times, produces a vast number of global arrangements. The exact exponent is not the point, and Susskind calls $10^{500}$ an old underestimate; the point is combinatorial proliferation.

p.src: Susskind then recalls an analogy from communication theory. Random codes can be extraordinarily good, while the codes easiest to describe and decode have extra mathematical structure and historically performed less well. Coding theory later found highly effective structured constructions, but the analogy remains: anything compactly named or described occupies a very special, low-complexity corner of the full space of possibilities. Likewise, the string vacua that are easiest to calculate may be atypically simple.

u.src: From Bricks to a Web of Descriptions
en: From Bricks to a Web of Descriptions
ja: レンガから記述の網へ
zh: 从砖块到描述之网

p.src: The hope that deeper layers of physics must be simpler has proved fragile. In $1+1$-dimensional bosonization, the same theory can be organized either around fermions or around bosons, with the fermion reappearing as a kink. In quantum electrodynamics, weak and strong coupling exchange the descriptive roles of electron and magnetic monopole. In string theory, F-strings and D-strings repeat the same pattern, and in the even-brane theory strong coupling goes further still: a compact direction expands, D0-branes become Kaluza–Klein momentum states, and effective strings are reinterpreted as wrapped membranes in a higher-dimensional geometry. Modern quantum field theory and string theory therefore do not furnish a unique once-and-for-all answer to the question which are the bricks and which are the houses? They furnish a web of descriptions, each efficient in its own regime, together with a huge landscape of possible constructions whose generic output is complexity rather than simplicity.

ja.text: 物理学のより深い層はより単純でなければならないという希望は、もろいものと判明した。

次元のボソン化では、同じ理論をフェルミオンを中心に組織することも、ボソンを中心に組織することもでき、フェルミオンはキンクとして再現する。量子電気力学では、弱結合と強結合が電子と磁気単極子の記述的役割を交換する。弦理論では、F弦とD弦が同じパターンを繰り返し、偶数ブレーン理論では強結合はさらに進む。コンパクトな方向が膨張し、D0ブレーンがKaluza–Klein運動量状態となり、有効弦がより高次元の幾何学における巻き付いた膜として再解釈される。したがって、現代の量子場の理論と弦理論は、
どちらがレンガでどちらが家か
という問いに対して、唯一の最終的な答えを与えるものではない。それらは、それぞれが自らの領域で効率的である記述の網と、可能な構成の巨大な景観とを与える。その一般的な出力は単純さではなく複雑さである。

zh.text: 认为物理学的更深层次必定更简单的希望已被证明是脆弱的。在
维玻色化中，同一理论既可以围绕费米子组织，也可以围绕玻色子组织，而费米子则作为扭结重新出现。在量子电动力学中，弱耦合与强耦合交换了电子与磁单极子的描述角色。在弦理论中，F弦与D弦重复了同样的模式，而在偶膜理论中，强耦合走得更远：一个紧致方向膨胀，D0膜变成Kaluza–Klein动量态，有效弦被重新解释为更高维几何中包裹的膜。因此，现代量子场论和弦理论并没有为
哪些是砖块，哪些是房屋？
这一问题提供唯一的、一劳永逸的答案。它们提供的是一张描述之网，每一种描述在各自的适用范围内都是高效的，同时还伴随着一个巨大的可能构造的景观，其普遍产物是复杂性而非简单性。
